terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive; passive obstupefīō
evidence: Ter. Ph. 2.1.54: eum timidum obstupefēcit pudor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To strike someone dumb with wonder (or with fear or shame).
Literally “thunderstruck”: the usual way to say “amazed” of people who stop dead.
To be dazed with astonishment; also, of the body, to be numb.

phrases.latin: veluti flammās spīrantium mīrāculō attonitī cōnstitērunt
phrases.english: they stood still, amazed at the wonder, as if the oxen were breathing fire
belched out, he comes forth amazed to be saved

sources: Lewis & Short: obstupefacio · Lewis & Short: attonitus · Lewis & Short: stupeo
